comments.content:
This is Ubuntu only and stuck
- no d/watch file to get newer source
- homepage points to https://openwsman.github.io/
- the test fail is in https://launchpadlibrarian.net/876762448/buildlog_ubuntu-stonking-amd64.openwsman_2.6.5-0ubuntu17_BUILDING.txt.gz and about cmake requirements being too old and compat was dropped
- no work on the package since many years other than automated rebuilds
- IMHO that would need to be a bump up from 2.6.5 (current in Ubuntu) to 2.8.1 (latest upstream)

=> https://github.com/Openwsman/openwsman/releases/tag/v2.8.1
=> Also the sibling wsmancli needs https://github.com/Openwsman/wsmancli/releases/tag/v2.8.0

bug.description:
## FFE ##

[Rationale]

* Without any fix this is an FTBFS, the FTBFS is because it is severely
  outdated not getting reasonable updates in many years.
  Upstream has continued to release new versions, they work, let us upgrade
  it to those to fix (alternative was to remove it, but MAAS still uses it)

[ Scope ]

* The two packages belong together (wsmancli uses openwsman) and are used
  by MAAS

* There are no other things directly depending on it

* The assumption would be that users would prefer a version of this decade :-)

* Add the output of seeded-in-ubuntu:

$ seeded-in-ubuntu wsmancli
wsmancli's binaries are not seeded.

Since the latest version is an FTBFS it would fail

$ seeded-in-ubuntu openwsman
Status unknown: No binary packages built by the latest openwsman.
Try again using -b and the expected binary packages.

But passing all binaries returns nothing either

$ seeded-in-ubuntu --binary libopenwsman-dev libopenwsman1 libwsman-client4t64 libwsman-client4t64-dbgsym libwsman-clientpp-dev libwsman-clientpp1t64 libwsman-clientpp1t64-dbgsym libwsman-curl-client-transport1 libwsman-curl-client-transport1-dbgsym libwsman-server1t64 libwsman-server1t64-dbgsym libwsman1t64 libwsman1t64-dbgsym openwsman openwsman-dbgsym

* For new upstream microreleases, include a diff of the upstream changelog
  since the version included in the archive. This could be a git
  commit log, CHANGES or NEWS file, or any other list of the relevant
  upstream changes.

[ Documentation ]

* There is no documentation for this package I could find other than
  package integrated man pages and such.

* Yes, updating this to a recent version may change the UX and we are past
  UI freeze, but I see no other feasible option to keep it alive right now.

[ Regression Potential ]

* After a decade of changes you'd expect much, but it is reasonably stable

* wsmancli only updated to be compatible to openwsman 2.8.0
  https://github.com/Openwsman/wsmancli/releases/tag/v2.8.0

* openwsman has gotten more, the patch versions are fixes, but 2.7 and 2.8 
  hold a few
  - https://github.com/Openwsman/openwsman/releases/tag/v2.7.0
  - https://github.com/Openwsman/openwsman/releases/tag/v2.8.0
  Calling out the two sets of API changes

* In regard to be "Tested" before an FFE I can't say much myself.
  This may need special hardware or at least spawn systems to talk.
  I can't do that. But since MAAS is the reason to need this
  instead of being removed I asked them to test the PPA.
  I'll wait with the upload until we get their answer here.

[ Testing ]

* Smoke test:
  - PPA: https://launchpad.net/~paelzer/+archive/ubuntu/lp-1867935-wsman-stonking
  - Build logs:
    - https://launchpadlibrarian.net/877756707/buildlog_ubuntu-stonking-amd64.openwsman_2.8.1-0ubuntu1~stonkingppa1_BUILDING.txt.gz
    - https://launchpadlibrarian.net/877803713/buildlog_ubuntu-stonking-amd64.wsmancli_2.8.0-0ubuntu1~stonkingppa1_BUILDING.txt.gz
  - Installation:

Update Sept 2026

This was Ubuntu only and broken just because no one was willing to update it.
Instead of a blunt removal (MAAS tells me they still use it) update it to the most recent version. I'm not adopting full maintainership, but tried to clean
up the packaging and move to a new version.

AFAICS:
- the new versions build
- match the latest upstream
- have some minor packaging improvements applied

PPA: https://launchpad.net/~paelzer/+archive/ubuntu/lp-1867935-wsman-stonking

That makes it need an FFE which is completed at the top of this.
